requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/annexes-page-439.tex:4
requirements.statement: Federates use the state of the object instances as one of the primary means of communication. At any point during a federation execution, at most one federate or the RTI shall have the privilege to update the value of a given object instance attribute. A joined federate that has the privilege to update values for an instance attribute is said to own that instance attribute. There are specific (MOM) instance attributes that are owned by the RTI. In some cases, an instance attribute may be unowned, neither owned by a federate nor the RTI. The Ownership Management services allow joined federates to gain ownership of unowned instance attributes, exchange ownership of instance attributes, or release ownership of instance attributes (possibly to become unowned). The federate provides instance attribute values to the other federates in the federation execution via Object Management services. The federate providing the instance attribute values is said to be updating that instance attribute. Federates receiving those values are said to be reflecting that instance attribute.%

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/annexes-page-439.tex:11
requirements.statement: Some of the arguments to the services described in this document are in the form of a group that represents some association. These groupings can take several forms (depending on the requirements of the respective service), each of which is described below. The groupings may be implemented slightly differently in each API, but all implementations shall support the same semantics. These groupings are pairs, sets, collections, constrained sets of pairs, and collections of pairs. Collections are sets that permit duplication of elements. They are used in cases in which duplication is unlikely and not really an error. As such, using a collection rather than a set retains the same effects, but without the expensive checks to eliminate duplicates that using a set would require. In these cases, it is preferred not to penalize the majority of users with the less efficient set just to catch errors that are anticipated to be infrequent.%

For example, in the Java API, the tag shall be an empty (zero-length) array. Examples of RTI-invoked services with empty user-supplied tags are Provide Attribute Value Update (via Auto Provide switch), Request Attribute Ownership (via Unconditional Divest resign directive), and MOM HLAmanager.HLAfederate.HLAreport interactions.%

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/annexes-page-439.tex:27
requirements.statement: The exact manner in which RTI-initiated services (callbacks) are invoked on a federate by the RTI is programming-language specific. However, the HLA defines two callback models that govern when callbacks may be invoked. The two callback models are: IMMEDIATE and EVOKED. In the IMMEDIATE model, the RTI shall invoke callbacks immediately when they are available, unless the callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. In the EVOKED model, callbacks are only made when the federate calls the Evoke Callback/Evoke Multiple Callbacks services, unless callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. RTIs shall implement both callback models. The callback model is specified as an argument to the Connect service.%

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/annexes-page-439.tex:4
requirements.statement: Once a federation execution exists, federates may join and resign from it in any sequence that is meaningful to the federation user. Figure 2 presents a generalized view of the basic relationship between a federate and the RTI during the federate participation in a federation execution. The broad arrows in Figure 2 represent the general invocation of HLA service groups and are not intended to demonstrate strict ordering requirements on the use of the services. An RTI shall allow an application to participate in a federation as multiple joined federates, and an RTI shall allow a single application to participate in multiple federations as a joined federate or federates.%

requirements.title: Federate Resigned reports involuntary resignation
requirements.statement: The Federate Resigned service shall notify a previously joined federate that it has resigned from the federation. The RTI shall invoke this service when the federate was resigned by any action except for the federate itself invoking Resign Federation Execution. The federate shall remain connected to the RTI. If a federate also disconnects from the RTI, a Federate Resigned service is not required to be sent. A Connection Lost service implies that the federate has resigned as well.
